title: In silico evaluation of bioactive compounds as potential inhibitors targeting HIF-1alpha/VEGFA/BACE1 pathway against Alzheimer's disease.
authors: Rai, Sakshi; Ray, Suman Kumar; Mukherjee, Sukhes
one_liner_zh: 该研究用分子对接和ADMET筛选靶向HIF-1alpha/VEGFA/BACE1的阿尔茨海默病抑制剂，虽涉及蛋白-小分子对接，但对象非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联弱。
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's disease (AD) are characterized by progressive neuronal degeneration, predominantly caused by the accumulation of amyloid-beta (Abeta) and neuroinflammatory processes. Hypoxia, characterized by diminished oxygen levels, intensifies these mechanisms by stimulating hypoxiainducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1alpha), potentially enhancing BACE1 enzyme activity and resulting in increased Abeta synthesis and render neurons especially susceptible to hypoxia, exacerbating disease progression. Existing therapies are constrained by inadequate medication distribution across the blood-brain barrier and associated adverse effects. This study aims to identify potential therapeutic agents targeting HIF-1alpha, VEGFA, BACE1 key molecules involved in AD by exploring neuroprotective effects of bioactive compounds like benzyl isothiocyanate (BITC), Aurantiamide Acetate (AA), and galantamine, with the goal of developing more effective, targeted treatments. METHODS: We used in silico screening, such as molecular docking and ADMET analysis, to assess the binding affinity, pharmacokinetics, and toxicity of potential inhibitors, followed by in vitro testing. RESULTS: Results identified several compounds with strong binding affinities and favorable ADMET profiles as potential inhibitors of HIF-1alpha, VEGFA, BACE1 and experimental data support that hypoxia, via HIF-1alpha, upregulates BACE1, increasing Abeta production and contributing to AD. Targeting these pathways may offer a multi-faceted approach to therapy, reducing neuroinflammation and amyloid pathology. CONCLUSIONS: In silico screening of potential molecules across different pathogenic pathways in Alzheimer's disease shows promise in developing successful therapeutic methods and continued validation may result in more tailored and safer medicines that address underlying neurodegenerative pathways.
abstract_zh: 目的：神经退行性疾病如阿尔茨海默病（AD）以进行性神经元退化为特征，主要由淀粉样蛋白-β（Abeta）积累和神经炎症过程引起。缺氧以氧水平降低为特征，通过刺激缺氧诱导因子1-α（HIF-1alpha）加剧这些机制，可能增强BACE1酶活性，导致Abeta合成增加，并使神经元对缺氧特别敏感，从而加剧疾病进展。现有疗法受限于药物在血脑屏障中的分布不足及相关不良反应。本研究旨在通过探索苄基异硫氰酸酯（BITC）、橙酰胺乙酸酯（AA）和加兰他敏等生物活性化合物的神经保护作用，识别靶向AD中关键分子HIF-1alpha、VEGFA、BACE1的潜在治疗药物，以期开发更有效、更具针对性的治疗方法。方法：我们使用计算机模拟筛选，如分子对接和ADMET分析，评估潜在抑制剂的结合亲和力、药代动力学和毒性，随后进行体外测试。结果：结果识别出几种具有强结合亲和力和良好ADMET特征的化合物，作为HIF-1alpha、VEGFA、BACE1的潜在抑制剂，实验数据支持缺氧通过HIF-1alpha上调BACE1，增加Abeta产生并促进AD。靶向这些通路可能提供多方面的治疗策略，减少神经炎症和淀粉样蛋白病理。结论：针对阿尔茨海默病不同致病通路的潜在分子计算机模拟筛选显示出开发成功治疗方法的潜力，持续验证可能产生更个性化和更安全的药物，以解决潜在的神经退行性通路。
